collegeReadiness.title: College Readiness & Retention

overview.summary: Approximately 32.9% of undergraduate students in the U.S. drop out of college each year, posing a significant challenge for the education sector.

keyConcerns.description: College dropout rates remain high, with many students not completing their degrees. Multiple sources confirm a substantial percentage leave before graduation.
The first year is especially critical, as a notable portion of students drop out before their sophomore year.
Community colleges generally have higher dropout rates than four-year universities. For-profit institutions tend to exhibit higher dropout rates compared to public or non-profit colleges.

dropoutFactors.description: Students often struggle to balance newfound independence, work, and social life

pandemicImpact.persistentChallenges: Student engagement, particularly in areas reliant on in-person interaction, has not fully returned to pre-pandemic levels. This includes challenges in collaborative learning, student-faculty interactions, and a sense of community.
pandemicImpact.learningBehaviors: There have been shifts in study habits and learning strategies, with increased reliance on digital resources and potentially less time spent in traditional library settings. The pandemic accelerated the adoption of online and hybrid learning, which has both benefits and drawbacks in terms of engagement.
pandemicImpact.socialEngagement: Social engagement, crucial for college students' development, has been significantly affected. Opportunities for informal interactions and community building have been reduced, impacting students' sense of belonging.
pandemicImpact.mentalHealthConcerns: Increased mental health challenges among college students further contribute to disengagement. Stress, anxiety, and isolation can make it difficult for students to focus and participate in academic activities.
pandemicImpact.variedImpacts: The impact of the pandemic on engagement varies among different student populations, with first-year students often facing greater challenges. Students' living situations, access to technology, and individual circumstances also play a role.

collegeReadiness.expanseRelevance: Expanse EDU's gamification and engagement strategies could help address college retention by building engagement habits in K-12 that transfer to higher education.

parentEngagement.expanseOpportunity: Expanse EDU can provide a bridge between parents and students through shared visibility into progress, achievements, and goals. Parent-configured rewards create collaborative goal-setting opportunities.

socialDynamics.title: Social Dynamics & Development

overview.summary: Research on how social interaction, play, and peer relationships affect development and learning.

keyFindings.detail: Reports of 'I feel lonely at school,' 'I feel like an outsider (or left out of things) at school,' and 'I make friends easily at school' have increased

keyFindings.insight: Our planet-changing trait was the ability to learn from each other
Play requires suppression of the drive to dominate and enables the formation of long-lasting cooperative bonds
Over time, they develop the social skills necessary for life in a democratic society, including self-governance, joint decision making, and accepting the outcome when you lose a contest

keyFindings.detail: Percentage of U.S. students (8th, 10th, and 12th grade) who meet up with friends 'almost every day' outside school has decreased

purposeAndMotivation.title: Purpose & Motivation in Education

overview.summary: Research shows that student motivation is deeply tied to perceived purpose and relevance of their education.
overview.source: Walton Family Foundation, Gallup, ECMC Group

keyFindings.stat: Less than half of middle and high school students reported feeling motivated to go to school
keyFindings.source: 2024 Walton Family Foundation and Gallup survey
keyFindings.cause: Lack of motivation is often linked to students not seeing the relevance of their coursework to their lives and future goals

keyFindings.stat: Less than half (45%) of students from traditionally underserved populations (low-income, first-generation, BIPOC) believe education after high school is necessary, compared to 52% of all high schoolers
keyFindings.implication: Significant disconnect between current schooling and perceived future needs

keyFindings.insight: When learning is connected to students' interests and future aspirations, they find their schoolwork more meaningful and tend to have higher academic achievement

purposeAndMotivation.expanseApproach: Expanse EDU connects learning to tangible rewards, visible progress, and real-world outcomes (scholarships, skills) to make education's value concrete and immediate.

engagementResearch.title: Student Engagement Research

overview.summary: Teachers, principals, parents, and districts all want their students engaged. Student engagement is shaped by a variety of interconnected factors.
overview.solution: Reversing the decline in engagement calls for a holistic strategy that emphasizes engaging instruction, supports student well-being, and connects learning to students' real-world experiences.

primary: Ongoing impacts of the COVID-19 pandemic, including disrupted learning and reduced social interaction
Curriculum misalignment with students' interests and perceived relevance
Emotional challenges such as stress, anxiety, and feeling undervalued
Overemphasis on grades rather than meaningful feedback
Evolving classroom dynamics and increased technology use
additional: Lack of Student Voice: Students often feel disengaged when they have little input
Limited Real-World Connections: Curriculum that doesn't connect to students' lives or future goals
Insufficient Support Services: Lack of access to counseling, mental health, or academic support
Overcrowded Classrooms: Large class sizes reduce individual attention
Socioeconomic Barriers: Financial stress, food insecurity, and unstable home environments
Cultural Disconnects: Curriculum and school culture that don't reflect students' backgrounds
High-Stakes Testing Pressure: Excessive focus on standardized tests creates stress
Teacher Burnout: Disengaged or overwhelmed teachers struggle to inspire students
Bullying and Social Exclusion: Negative peer interactions make school feel unsafe
Lack of Extracurricular Opportunities: Limited access to clubs, sports, or creative outlets

keyStatistics.stat: 74% of fifth graders are highly engaged vs ~33% of high schoolers
keyStatistics.implication: Massive engagement drop-off as students progress through school

keyStatistics.breakdown: Less than half are actively engaged

keyStatistics.stat: Engaged students are 2.5x more likely to say they get excellent grades
Engaged students are 4.5x more likely to be hopeful about the future

attentionSpan.trend: Average human attention span decreased from 12 seconds in 2000 to 8 seconds in 2013
attentionSpan.comparison: Shorter than a goldfish's reported 9-second attention span

causes.detail: Continuous stream of rapid, fragmented content on platforms like TikTok, Snapchat, and Instagram overstimulates cognitive processes
Young people (16-24) often engage with multiple screens simultaneously, eroding capacity for deep, sustained focus
Digital platforms provide instant gratification through likes, notifications, and endless scrolling, training the brain to seek constant novelty

attentionSpan.academicConsequences: Shorter attention spans are linked to poorer test performance, difficulty retaining long-term information, and struggles in connecting ideas into cohesive understanding

engagementResearch.autonomyEffect: When individuals have the freedom to make choices and take ownership of their work, they often feel more motivated and invested in their tasks. This sense of control fosters a deeper connection to their work, leading to greater creativity, productivity, and overall satisfaction.
